feed.title: EuropeDoor stories
feed.subtitle: A continent is people before it is places. Nine essays, filed to nine desks.
feed.rights: Editorial text is EuropeDoor's own. Reproduce with attribution and a link.

entry.title: The long walk nobody finishes
entry.summary: Europe has four trails over a thousand kilometres long. Almost everyone who starts one stops, and the ones who plan to stop have a better time than the ones who do not.

entry.title: The ferry is the attraction
entry.summary: Some of Europe’s best journeys are public transport, priced as public transport, and almost nobody treats them as sightseeing.

entry.title: The city rebuilt from paintings
entry.summary: Warsaw’s old town is a reconstruction, and UNESCO listed it precisely for that.

entry.title: The languages with no relatives
entry.summary: Basque, Hungarian, Finnish, Georgian and Albanian have almost nothing in common except that they do not fit.

entry.title: The case for going in October
entry.summary: Europe’s crowding problem is not the number of visitors. It is that they all arrive in the same eleven places in the same six weeks.

entry.title: The cheese that explains a country
entry.summary: You can read a European landscape backwards from what it makes: altitude, rainfall, grass and who owned the land.

entry.title: What a pilgrimage is for when you do not believe
entry.summary: Three hundred thousand people a year walk to Santiago. Most of them do not describe the reason as religious, and the Camino has absorbed that without much difficulty.

entry.title: The bridge that was rebuilt from its own river
entry.summary: Mostar’s Stari Most stood for 427 years, fell in 1993, and came back out of the water it fell into.

entry.title: The last forest that was never cut
entry.summary: Białowieża has never been logged, which in Europe makes it a survivor of something the rest of the continent lost quietly and without noticing.
